claims.statement: KPV (Lys-Pro-Val) is the C-terminal tripeptide fragment of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH(11-13)), with PubChem CID 125672, CAS number 67727-97-3, and molecular formula C16H30N4O4.

claims.statement: In vitro, nanomolar concentrations of KPV inhibit NF-kappaB and MAP kinase inflammatory signaling and reduce pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion in human intestinal epithelial cell lines and T cells, and KPV is taken up into cells via the peptide transporter PepT1.

context.population: in vitro human cell lines (Caco2-BBE, HT29-Cl.19A intestinal epithelial cells; Jurkat T cells)

extractedEvidence.quote: Nanomolar concentrations of KPV inhibit the activation of NF-kappaB and MAP kinase inflammatory signaling pathways, and reduce pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion.
This study indicates that KPV is transported into cells by PepT1 and might be a new therapeutic agent for IBD.

reviewFlags: in vitro mechanism finding; must not be presented as a confirmed human mechanism of action

claims.statement: In C57BL/6 mouse models of DSS- and TNBS-induced colitis, oral administration of KPV in drinking water reduced colitis incidence and inflammatory markers (including myeloperoxidase activity and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression); this is an animal-model finding, not evidence of efficacy in humans.

context.population: C57BL/6 mice (DSS and TNBS chemically-induced colitis models)
context.doseText: Approximately 100 micromolar KPV in drinking water in mouse colitis models (animal-study protocol; not a human dosing recommendation).

extractedEvidence.quote: In vivo experiments administered KPV orally via drinking water at 100 micromolar concentration in two colitis models.

reviewFlags: animal-only efficacy signal; per directive, must not be inferred as proven human efficacy
dose context is an animal-study protocol dose and must never be presented as a human use recommendation

claims.statement: FDA lists KPV in the 'bulk drug substances nominated but withdrawn' table for 503A compounding evaluation, stating it has not identified any human exposure data for KPV administered via any route and lacks information on whether KPV would cause harm if administered to humans.

extractedEvidence.quote: FDA has not identified any human exposure data on drug products containing KPV administered via any route of administration. FDA lacks important information regarding any safety issues raised by KPV, including whether it would cause harm if administered to humans.

reviewFlags: withdrawn-nomination status means KPV is not currently under active FDA 503A evaluation; confirm this has not changed at review time, since FDA revised several peptide listings in April 2026

claims.statement: No completed human clinical trials of KPV have been identified; published efficacy and mechanism evidence for KPV's anti-inflammatory effects is limited to animal (mouse) colitis and dermatitis models and in vitro human cell-line experiments, leaving human efficacy and safety for gut-health, skin, and general anti-inflammatory uses unestablished despite active consumer marketing of KPV for those uses.

context.route: oral, subcutaneous, or topical (as commonly marketed)
context.formulation: research-grade KPV, often combined with other peptides (e.g., GHK-Cu)
context.useCase: gut health, skin/anti-inflammatory, general wellness marketing claims
